questions.title: Analyse a business
questions.prompt: I enjoy working out how a company makes money and what drives its value.
questions.hint: Try comparing the revenue drivers of two businesses.

questions.title: Form an investment view
questions.prompt: I enjoy following markets, weighing evidence and revising an investment view.
questions.hint: Try explaining what would change a view you currently hold.

questions.title: Understand a client
questions.prompt: I enjoy listening to someone’s needs and building a working relationship.
questions.hint: Think about a time you clarified what another person really needed.

questions.title: Work mathematically
questions.prompt: I enjoy probability, statistics and explaining mathematical assumptions.
questions.hint: Think about solving a problem and checking why the method applies.

questions.title: Build with code
questions.prompt: I enjoy programming, debugging and testing data or software.
questions.hint: Rate the task itself, even if your current skill level is early.

questions.title: Coordinate a transaction
questions.prompt: I enjoy detailed, deadline-driven projects involving several stakeholders.
questions.hint: Think about organising information, revisions and hand-offs.

questions.title: Challenge a risk
questions.prompt: I enjoy questioning a proposed decision and investigating what could go wrong.
questions.hint: Think about a useful challenge supported by evidence.

questions.title: Decide as information moves
questions.prompt: I enjoy responding to fast-changing information and making timely decisions.
questions.hint: Distinguish enjoying the pace from simply tolerating pressure.

questions.title: Make a process reliable
questions.prompt: I enjoy checking details, investigating mismatches and preventing repeat errors.
questions.hint: Think about catching a problem and improving the process.

questions.title: Explain a recommendation
questions.prompt: I enjoy turning complex information into a clear, defensible recommendation.
questions.hint: Think about adapting an explanation to a particular audience.

roles.name: Investment banking
roles.work: Advise companies and financial sponsors on transactions and financing. Analyst work can involve research, financial modelling, valuation, presentations and managing transaction details.
roles.overlap: Corporate finance and private markets share company analysis and valuation. Banking advises clients on transactions; investors decide whether to commit capital.
roles.future: Research corporate advisory, capital markets or sector coverage. Later moves depend on experience, performance and available roles.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain financial statements, enterprise versus equity value and one valuation approach.

roles.name: Asset management
roles.work: Research investments and build or support portfolios for clients. Work varies by asset class and may combine company analysis, macro research, portfolio construction and risk monitoring.
roles.overlap: Equity research develops investment views; risk teams challenge exposures. Portfolio management adds allocation, sizing and client mandate constraints.
roles.future: Explore research analyst, investment specialist, multi-asset or portfolio support routes. Portfolio responsibility normally develops with experience.
roles.prepare: Start here: compare two investments and discuss return drivers, risks and portfolio fit.

roles.name: Wealth management
roles.office: CLIENT & INVESTMENT ROLES / OFTEN FRONT OFFICE
roles.work: Help individuals and families organise investments and financial objectives. Roles can focus on relationship management, investment advice, portfolio management or financial planning.
roles.overlap: Asset management shares investment analysis. Wealth adds personal circumstances, suitability, client communication and longer-term relationships.
roles.future: Explore assistant relationship manager, investment analyst and planning pathways. Advice responsibilities depend on training and regulatory permissions.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain risk tolerance, diversification and how you would clarify a client’s needs.

roles.name: Risk management
roles.work: Identify, measure and challenge exposures such as market, credit, liquidity and operational risk. Work can range from data analysis and modelling to limits, governance and reporting.
roles.overlap: Quant, treasury, compliance and investment teams all use risk information. Independent risk has a distinct challenge and oversight role.
roles.future: Explore market, credit, model or enterprise risk. Career paths depend on technical depth, product knowledge and the kind of risk you specialise in.
roles.prepare: Start here: describe a loss scenario, its drivers, controls and the limits of a risk measure.

roles.name: Sales & trading
roles.work: Support clients’ market activity through sales, trading, structuring or execution. Tasks depend on product and desk, and combine market knowledge, communication, risk and pricing.
roles.overlap: Research informs views; quant supports models and pricing; risk provides oversight. Sales and trading are distinct roles with different daily emphasis.
roles.future: Explore desk-specific sales, trading, structuring and electronic markets. Product knowledge and client needs shape progression.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain a recent market move and how it could affect a client or trading position.

roles.name: Quantitative finance
roles.office: FRONT OR MIDDLE OFFICE / TEAM DEPENDENT
roles.work: Use mathematics, statistics and programming to analyse data, model products or develop investment and risk methods. Quant research, development and model validation are different jobs.
roles.overlap: Trading, systematic investing, risk and technology share coding and models. The objective and who uses the model determine the role.
roles.future: Explore quant research, pricing, model validation or quantitative development. Entry requirements can be substantially mathematical.
roles.prepare: Start here: implement a small model, explain its assumptions and test its behaviour.

roles.name: Equity & credit research
roles.work: Analyse companies, industries or issuers and form a reasoned view. Equity research focuses on ownership and valuation; credit research focuses on repayment, downside and debt terms.
roles.overlap: Banking also analyses companies, while asset management uses research to make portfolio decisions. Research depth, audience and incentives differ.
roles.future: Explore sell-side or buy-side research, sector coverage and credit analysis. Moving to portfolio roles requires further investment responsibility.
roles.prepare: Start here: build a short investment or credit thesis with valuation, risks and what would change your view.

roles.name: Private equity & venture capital
roles.work: Assess investments in private companies, support due diligence and monitor portfolio businesses. Buyout, growth and venture strategies have very different investment criteria.
roles.overlap: Banking shares transaction and valuation skills. Venture can emphasise markets, founders and growth; buyouts place greater weight on cash flow, leverage and operations.
roles.future: Explore investment and portfolio-support roles. Direct undergraduate opportunities exist but vary; prior transaction or operating experience can matter.
roles.prepare: Start here: assess a business model, investment rationale, main risks and due-diligence questions.

roles.name: Corporate banking
roles.work: Work with companies on lending, cash management and related banking services. Roles connect credit analysis, sector understanding, client needs and relationship management.
roles.overlap: Investment banking focuses more on transactions and capital markets; corporate banking often centres on ongoing banking relationships and credit.
roles.future: Explore coverage, credit analysis and product teams. Experience can lead to relationship management or more specialised financing work.
roles.prepare: Start here: assess a company’s ability to service debt and explain a relevant banking need.

roles.name: Treasury
roles.office: CORPORATE FINANCE OR BANK TREASURY / VARIES
roles.work: Manage cash, liquidity, funding and financial exposures. Corporate treasury supports a business; bank treasury manages the institution’s balance sheet and funding needs.
roles.overlap: Risk measures exposures; finance reports performance; markets teams execute instruments. Treasury connects those functions to liquidity and funding decisions.
roles.future: Explore cash management, liquidity, asset-liability management or funding. Responsibilities depend on the organisation.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain cash versus profit and how interest-rate or currency risk affects a business.

roles.name: FP&A & corporate finance
roles.office: INTERNAL FINANCE / OFFICE LABELS OFTEN UNHELPFUL
roles.work: Support business decisions through budgeting, forecasts, performance analysis and financial planning. Some corporate finance teams also handle investment appraisal and transactions.
roles.overlap: Accounting provides actual results; strategy sets direction; treasury manages cash and funding. FP&A turns financial information into operating decisions.
roles.future: Explore financial analyst, business partnering and planning roles. Broader finance leadership normally requires substantial experience.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain a variance, forecast a driver and turn the result into a business recommendation.

roles.name: Actuarial
roles.work: Use statistics and financial modelling to assess uncertain long-term costs and risks. Work may cover insurance pricing, reserving, capital, pensions or investment advice.
roles.overlap: Risk and quant share modelling; consulting adds client communication. Actuarial work has its own professional qualification and practice context.
roles.future: Explore insurance, pensions, investment consulting or risk routes. Qualification requirements and study support vary by employer.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain a probability model, its assumptions and how you would communicate uncertainty.

roles.name: Compliance & financial crime
roles.work: Help firms understand obligations, manage conduct and financial-crime risks, and monitor controls. Compliance, legal and internal audit are related but separate functions.
roles.overlap: Risk, operations and business teams implement controls. Compliance interprets and challenges conduct and regulatory processes; audit independently evaluates them.
roles.future: Explore advisory compliance, monitoring, anti-money laundering or sanctions. Specialisation follows the business and regulatory area.
roles.prepare: Start here: work through a control failure, evidence requirements and a sensible escalation path.

roles.name: Operations & trade support
roles.office: OFTEN BACK OR MIDDLE OFFICE / VARIES
roles.work: Make financial activity work reliably: settlements, reconciliations, asset servicing, collateral and exception management. Some roles sit close to desks; others support firm-wide processing.
roles.overlap: Trading initiates activity; technology builds systems; operations ensures records and processes reconcile and issues are resolved.
roles.future: Explore product operations, trade support, control and process improvement. Moves across functions depend on demonstrated skills and opportunities.
roles.prepare: Start here: explain a trade lifecycle, investigate a mismatch and propose a control.

roles.name: Finance technology & data
roles.work: Build and maintain software, data pipelines and analytical tools used by financial firms. Engineering, data science, analytics and production support have different responsibilities.
roles.overlap: Quant uses models; operations needs reliable workflows; every business needs sound data. Technology focuses on robust systems and delivery.
roles.future: Explore software engineering, data engineering, analytics and platform roles. Product knowledge can complement technical expertise.
roles.prepare: Start here: build a small data workflow with clear documentation, checks and reproducible output.

roles.name: Financial services consulting
roles.work: Help financial institutions solve strategy, risk, technology or operational problems. Work often combines research, analysis, stakeholder conversations and recommendations.
roles.overlap: Specialist risk, finance and technology knowledge can be used in advisory work. Consultants support a client’s decision rather than owning every ongoing function.
roles.future: Explore specialist consulting teams and project delivery. Later paths depend on the capabilities and industry knowledge you build.
roles.prepare: Start here: structure an ambiguous problem, prioritise analysis and present a defensible recommendation.
